Prosecutrix is elder daughter of the complainant aged about 11 years (minor).

On 22/11/2017, complainant Sujata Rajput (PW-2)
mother of prosecutrix lodged a complaint at Police Station Kotwali, Vidisha at Crime No.829/2017 alleging that on the fateful day, when she returned from the Market, her daughter (prosecutrix) told her that when she went to Market, then her father (present appellant) committed rape over her.

complainant called her mother and narrated the incident, then they reported the incident at Police Station.

sentences.text: After recording of evidence, ocular as well as documentary and hearing the submissions of counsel for the parties, trial Court convicted and sentenced the appellant/accused person as referred above.
Therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7475 4 CRA-4847-2019 appellant is before this Court.
11. It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that trial Court erred in convicting the appellant for the offence referred above.
There is material contradictions and omissions between the statements of prosecution witnesses.

The statement of complainant (PW-2) was not vetted by the trial Court as on the one hand while lodging the FIR and in her statements recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., she stated that prosecutrix told her that appellant used to commit rape over her for last 03 months whereas in her cross-examination, she stated that appellant used to commit rape for last 04-05 months, which itself is contradictory.
Such aspects have not been considered by the trial Court while convicting the appellant.

12. It is further submitted that appellant and complainant are husband and wife and there are some marital dispute between both of them and to take vengeance, she used their daughter as weapon and lodged false case against him whereas, prosecutrix is his daughter.

13. It is further submitted that medical report prepared by Dr. Pratibha Oswal (PW-5) does not suggest commission of any such offence as there is no injuries either internal or external over the private parts of the prosecutrix.
Due to marital dispute, complainant falsely implicated the appellant in the case.
Only on the basis of conjecture and surmises, appellant has been held guilty by the trial Court which is not correct.
Thus, the trial Court committed grave error in convicting the appellant under Sections 376(2)(f)(i)(n) and Section 506 part II of IPC and Section 5(l)(m)(n) and Section 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

Thus, prayed for setting aside of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:7475 5 CRA-4847-2019 impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the trial Court.
Alternatively, learned counsel for the appellant submits that since appellant suffered around 08 years and 05 months and is first offender, therefore, some lenient view may be adopted.
1 4 . On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
It is further submitted that prosecutrix was minor and daughter of present appellant and she herself stated that appellant used to commit rape with her.

He further submits that present case is very sensitive in nature because here accused/appellant is father and prosecutrix is his daughter and act done by the appellant does not set a fine image of a father towards her daughter in the society.
Prosecution witnesses supported the story of prosecution and remained unshaken.
Therefore, trial Court did not err in convicting the appellant for the offence as referred above.
Therefore, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

15. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
16.
This is a case of rape allegedly committed by the appellant, who happens to be father of the prosecutrix (who was minor).

From the FIR lodged on 22/11/2017, it appears that rape was committed by the appellant (father of the prosecutrix) over the prosecutrix, who happens to be girl Ram Kishan Rajput vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130183169/

sentences.text: aged about 11 years
. As alleged, rape was committed for last 03 months regularly.
Looking to the peculiar nature of allegations where prosecutrix is victim but complainant is her mother

, therefore,
allegations are to be seen from that ventage point.
When offence is of rape then medical examination of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7475 6 CRA-4847-2019 prosecutrix assumes importance.

17. Dr. Pratibha Oswal (PW-5) examined prosecutrix vide Ex.P/4 and in the report, she mentioned the fact that neither any marks of injuries over private parts of the prosecutrix were found, nor any tenderness or bleeding was found.
Therefore, no definite opinion could have been given regarding intercourse with the prosecutrix.
Age of the prosecutrix was found by Dr. (PW-5) as 10-12 years and mensuratal cycle of prosecutrix was not started.

When such opinion in specific terms is given by the Dr. (PW-5), then this opinion assumes importance because if a girl aged 10-12 years of tender age would have been subjected to such physical/ sexual violence then certain injuries ought to have been sustained by her (external/ internal injuries) over her private parts but in the present case, no such injuries were found over person of the prosecutrix.
In her testimony, prosecutrix (PW-1) specifically mentioned the fact that she was subjected to rape by her father and she narrated the incident accordingly.
If testimony of prosecutrix is true, then it is apparent that injuries ought to had been found over the person/ private parts of the prosecutrix.
But no such injury was found by doctor.

1 8 . Another aspect in the present case assumes importance is that DNA test of the prosecutrix was not conducted by the Investigating Officer, whereas samples were referred to RFSL Bhopal for FSL report.
DNA test could have been done then and there only.
That could have been a good corroborative piece of evidence.
In absence of any DNA test, the Court has to rely upon the medical report and attending facts and circumstances of the case.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7475 7 CRA-4847-2019 19.
Prosecutrix (PW-1) admits in her statement that there was a dispute between her parents (appellant and complainant).
In para 3 of her cross- examination, prosecutrix categorically admits that her mother and father used to quarrel regularly.
She also mentioned the fact that her mother lodged 2-3 reports earlier also at police station against her father.

Even at family counselling center,
their dispute was tried to be resolved.
20. Prosecutrix further elaborated that sometimes her father used to consume alcohol and beat her mother.
Suggestions were given to the prosecutrix about modus operandi adopted by her mother to implicate her father so as to get rid of her father.
Although some suggestions were not admitted by the witness, but all possible suggestions regarding dispute existing between the couple were raised by the defence.
21. Not only this, mother of the prosecutrix (PW-2) also admits that she is having dispute with her husband (present appellant) and she lodged a complaint at police Station Kotwali against him.

Complainant (PW-2) however, admits that before 22/11/2017 (date on which FIR was lodged),
prosecutrix never made any complaint to her as regards such incident whereas in her cross-examination, complainant referred the fact that her daughter told her about such sexual Ram Kishan Rajput vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 26 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130183169/
4 violence allegedly committed by her husband over her for last 04-05 months.

sentences.text: This is improvement in her own version of FIR and statements recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., because earlier in FIR/ statement, she referred 03 months' period during which rape was allegedly committed.

2 2 . From the testimonies of complainant (PW-2) as well as Smt. NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:7475 8 CRA-4847-2019 Shanti Bai (PW-3) mother of complainant, it appears that appellant and his wife (complainant) entered into wedlock not by following Saptapadi Rituals but it was a love marriage performed in a temple by putting garlands over each other.

Incidentally,
when they entered into wedlock, mother of prosecutrix was carrying pregnancy of 06 months.

Therefore, as per the story of defence just to remove the appellant from her way, this conspiracy was hatched so that she could have settled with another person and when all dots are connected then this stand taken by the defence appears to be justified.

23. Another aspect regarding delay in lodging the FIR also assumes importance because as per the FIR, sexual violence was allegedly committed for last 03 months and as per the testimony of the complainant (PW-2), said incident was repeated regularly for last 04-05 months (before lodging the FIR), then such delay also assumes importance when seen collectively and cumulatively.

Normally,
delay in lodging the FIR does not mean that the doubt is to be raised about the allegations but certainly other attending facts and circumstances are to be seen and in that perspective, in the present case, delay in lodging the FIR assumes importance.

24. In the considered opinion of this Court, when medical examination belies the allegations and no iota of evidence exists so far as medical examination is concerned and theory of dispute between the couple is established then in that backdrop, prosecution could not prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.
Therefore, case of prosecution faulters and said benefit ought to have been given to the appellant/ accused.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7475 9 CRA-4847-2019 2 5 .

Resultantly, instant appeal preferred by the appellant is hereby allowed and judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 08/05/2019 passed by Second Additional Sessions Judge/ Special Judge (POCSO Act), Vidisha in SC No.06/2018 is hereby set aside.
